claims.statement: Commands are registered at compile time in src-tauri/build.rs via tauri_build::AppManifest::new().commands([...]) listing all 20 command names, generating IPC bindings.

Every command has an explicit allow-* permission in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json (e.g., allow-compute-diff-cmd, allow-open-file), ensuring a narrow, auditable command surface in packaged builds.

The DesktopAPI interface in src/platform/desktop.ts wraps all 20 Tauri commands with typed signatures, using @tauri-apps/api/core::invoke() with snake_case command names and camelCase argument objects matching Rust parameter names.

getDesktopAPI() returns the Tauri implementation when isTauri() is true, a pre-injected window.desktopAPI for testing, or undefined on the web, enabling graceful degradation to browser fallbacks (file input, local diff, highlight.js).

Rust command handlers validate all arguments: file operations use native dialogs with path checks, diff commands enforce 5 MiB/10k line limits via validate_input_cmd, history enforces 1 MiB per side and 20 MiB total, and open_recent_file verifies the path is still in the recent list.

Web fallback mirrors Rust limits in src/utils/limits.ts and uses local implementations: computeDiff() for diff, highlight.js for syntax highlighting, and <input type="file"> for file operations; recent files and history are unavailable on web.
